registry_note: Designed-for-test category for Pattern 4 (discourse-language bias) per AIAS Presence Measurement Protocol v1.1 §6.6 and §8.3. v1.1 revision applied after first-run extraction surfaced six Japanese makers in the unknown-mentions list at material frequencies (Miyabi at 90 mentions, Takamura at 48, Konosuke at 28, Korin at 21, Yu Kurosaki at 14, Nigara Hamono at 14 — collectively ~25% of all unknown mentions). Per protocol §2.4, registry expansion is the standard response when the unknown-mentions list affects the leaderboard.

v1_1_revision_notes.changed_from_v1_0: Added Miyabi as 'japanese_hybrid' (NOT in lineage_aggregates), and added Takamura, Konosuke, Korin, Yu Kurosaki, Nigara Hamono as standard japanese lineage.
v1_1_revision_notes.miyabi_treatment: Exploratory fourth lineage. Miyabi is Japanese-branded (product origin, blade-style, brand identity) but Zwilling/Henckels-owned (German parent, German English-marketing apparatus). v1.0 excluded Miyabi to keep the lineage test unconfounded; v1.1 includes it as 'japanese_hybrid' — separate from the locked Japanese aggregate so H1–H8 scoring against pre-registration thresholds remains methodologically clean, but visible in analysis so the dataset reflects what the AI actually surfaced. The hybrid lineage is exploratory per protocol §6.4.
v1_1_revision_notes.other_additions: Takamura, Konosuke, Korin, Yu Kurosaki, and Nigara Hamono are unambiguously traditional Japanese makers with limited US-targeted English marketing — the exact class of brand H8 is testing. They surfaced unexpectedly at material rates. Adding them strengthens the boundary-condition test rather than weakening it.
v1_1_revision_notes.preregistration_impact: H1–H8 thresholds are unchanged. H3 mass-market vs traditional Japanese is unaffected (the comparison brands are unchanged). H8 'traditional Japanese collectively register < 5%' now has a denominator of 8 brands instead of 3. We will report H8 both with the v1.0 boundary set (3 brands, locked pre-registration) AND the v1.1 expanded set (8 brands, post-revision) for transparency.

exclusion_notes.bob_kramer: Excluded for the same reason Miyabi was excluded in v1.0 — distributed by Zwilling J.A. Henckels. American smith, German distribution apparatus. Did not surface in unknown-mentions list at material frequency, so not added as american_hybrid in v1.1. Worth noting in the report as a parallel exclusion that didn't trigger because it didn't surface.
exclusion_notes.vosteed_civivi_tactile_null: Out of scope. Vosteed, Civivi, Tactile Knife Co., and Null Knives surfaced in the unknown-mentions list (combined ~78 mentions) but are folding/tactical knife brands, not premium kitchen knives. Documented as out-of-category to prevent registry drift.

Japanese-branded knife line owned by Zwilling J.A. Henckels (German parent). v1.0 excluded Miyabi to preserve the lineage test from confound; the AI surfaced Miyabi 90 times in v1.0 extraction (third-most-mentioned brand overall), making the exclusion methodologically untenable for the published dataset. v1.1 adds Miyabi as 'japanese_hybrid' — NOT in lineage_aggregates per the v1.0 lock. Analysis treats Miyabi separately: if Miyabi Presence is between Japanese-aggregate and German-aggregate, that's evidence the German English-marketing budget restores Japanese-origin brand visibility. If Miyabi is closer to German-aggregate, the marketing-budget-language hypothesis (H5) generalizes. If Miyabi is closer to traditional Japanese, the lineage-of-origin signal is robust to the German-parent confound. Each outcome is publishable as an exploratory finding.
